subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support a Docker sandbox recovery path for hosts where `--security-opt no-new-privileges` prevents even `/usr/bin/sleep` from execing?
rationale: The bug is well isolated, but removing or falling back from `no-new-privileges` changes the Docker sandbox boundary and repository policy requires explicit operator-controlled security tradeoffs rather than silent compatibility fallback.

options.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
options.body: Keep the secure default, add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

options.title: Diagnostic-only recovery
options.body: Keep the hardening unconditional and improve startup/session/doctor errors so affected hosts get a precise explanation and mitigation guidance without weakening the sandbox.

options.title: Unsupported host stance
options.body: Treat Docker hosts that reject `no-new-privileges` as unsupported for Docker sandbox mode and direct users to another sandbox backend or host configuration.

recommendation.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the secure default, add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history on sandbox dangerous-override and Docker create-args patterns that this decision would extend.
